posts.text: Idk if FinTwit even exists anymore as the LLM lemming content brigade, whom has created a biz of repurposing smarter folks actual work in an attempt to act like they have any clue about underlying mechanics of neural networks, temporal knowledge graphs, what a cache token is even (maybe lol), etc. all In a cheap attempt to hijack your attention and gain a following. Their are legions of these folks who do this at an industrial scale and have literally no shame. They are people looking for an arbitrage to elevate their status without doing the real work, but as someone who ran a really amazing arbitrage strategy for years I will let it slide. The world is competitive and the legacy winners keep creating more oats to entrench their N-h winnings and make sure they persist - can’t hate on anyone trying to escape feudalism. Having said all that and if you made it this far here is one the greatest quotes in finance of all-time from one of the great financial philosophers who owns a lot of the best quotes and ideas about finance, economies, and beauty contests 👙 - the misunderstood titan then and since JMK. “Practical men who believe themselves to be quite exempt from any intellectual influence, are usually the slaves of some defunct economist. Madmen in authority, who hear voices in the air, are distilling their frenzy from some academic scribbler of a few years back.” Think about this quote a bit and then the next time you spout off about some dumb fucking idea like sharpe ratio or capital market line or stationary beta or any stateless financial concept that was simply stolen from physics and then shoved down your throat even after the frontier thinkers falsified it I would implore you to ask yourself - “what do I really know and why I am playing a game where an unobservable mythical terminal constitutes the majority of the value of the claim on money that I exchanged my real money for to gain that asset, aka claim on money not to be confused with a real asset. And if you want to give me some shit quote then ask yourself the last time you swapped your stock for a physical / real asset? I would love to see a study that shows what % of ownership is traded for true assets. I would guess it’s close to the minima on the L’Hopital rule lower limit if you remember that Frenchmen’s addition to calculus. Ask yourself if you believe this young highly intelligent and very well funded wunderkid ever thought one second about terminal value or just simply subscribed to the current religion of “follow price” - an entire legion of Fremen in markets today. We know how this ends. Think about it if SPX goes to 10k by 2028 but then tests the capitalism line doing a 2/3 of your bezzle capital then what is better - take a chill pill now (ish) and monetize the bezzle of this insane move since March 2023 and the. earn 4.25% vanilla on your cash net of taxes or convince yourself you don’t want to pay the 20% but risk an entropic event that could cost your 2.5-3.5x that fealty to the Trumpster? I mean as aside no one should pay taxes into a regime that exhibits behavior that shows literally zero respect for you as a citizen. Let’s see how the govt is really willing to push the deficit to protect the status quo while simultaneously risking stability of the system. We truly live in insane times. The logical follow through is ask yourself what passive owners do when the gravy train consensus shifts? What do pod shop vest wearing bros do? What do trend followers do? Legit, my old HF partner who is one of the best long investors of all time might be the only guy sitting there to buy. Just the way he likes it and why he’s is the best you have never heard of - the new game is choosing to run the trend or buy negative correlation while being long. Xo Benny Just a thought experiment for you to think about and a little Keynes quote to pepper all the young bucks who never read the goat and inspire some Curiosity.
